answer: Random roll calls make each fake key cost a live model. Every epoch the beacon, a public random draw published after the epoch starts, names 10 percent of rewarded keys, and all of them get the same fresh task at the same second. Each must answer within the zephyr, a 3-second window, too short for one model to serve many keys in turn. A key that misses goes on the comet list and its rewards stay frozen for 20 epochs. Since a farm cannot know which keys the beacon picks, all 1,000 fakes need a model ready at once, so the farm pays for 1,000 concurrent instances.
